q: In the pre-merger financial structure of the Railways, the balance remaining after meeting the working expenses, the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund and the dividend payable to General Revenues was treated as the:

options.C: Surplus of the Railways, available for appropriation to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund

e: In the pre-merger structure, the balance left after working expenses, appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Pension Fund and dividend to General Revenues was the surplus. This surplus was appropriated to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund.

q: While compiling the gross working expenses of a zonal railway for a year, a clerk leaves out the appropriation made during the year to the Pension Fund, treating it as a mere book adjustment outside working expenses. The correct position is that the gross working expenses comprise the ordinary working expenses together with the appropriations to:

options.A: The Development Fund and the Capital Fund only
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund
options.D: No fund at all, appropriations being excluded from working expenses

e: Gross Working Expenses comprise Ordinary Working Expenses plus appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund. These appropriations are real revenue charges for asset renewal and pension liability, so leaving out the Pension Fund understates the total.

q: At the close of a month, the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' of a zonal railway shows a debit balance. This debit balance represents:

options.A: Cheques deposited with the bank which have not yet been realised
options.B: Cheques issued by the railway which have not yet been paid by the bank
options.C: Cash held in the chest of the Cash and Pay Office

e: A debit balance under Cheques and Bills represents cheques deposited with the bank which have not yet been realised and credited. Cheques issued but unpaid by the bank would appear on the opposite side as amounts still payable by the railway.

q: Wages have been earned by the staff of a zonal railway for the last days of a month but remain unpaid at the close of that month. Pending actual payment in the following month, the amount of such wages is held in the books under the debt head:
e: Wages earned but unpaid at the close of a month cannot be left unaccounted, as working expenses are booked on accrual. The amount is held under the debt head Unpaid Wages pending actual payment in the following month, when the head is cleared.

q: A debit balance under the head 'Miscellaneous Advances' in the books of a zonal railway represents:

options.A: Advances made by the railway which are recoverable, or adjustable to the final heads of account, in due course
options.B: Amounts due to outside suppliers for goods already received
options.C: Deposits received from contractors and held by the railway
options.D: Earnings collected at stations but not yet remitted to the bank

e: Miscellaneous Advances is a debt head for amounts advanced by the railway which are recoverable in cash or adjustable to final heads in due course. A debit balance under it therefore represents outstanding recoverable advances, not amounts owed to suppliers.

q: One zonal railway raises a debit against another zonal railway through a transfer transaction and expects the respondent railway to adjust the amount straightaway in its books without its concurrence. The correct position is that the transfer debit takes effect in the books of the respondent railway only on its:

options.B: Reference of the matter to the Railway Board in every case
options.C: Acceptance of the debit raised against it
options.D: Silence for a period of three years

e: A transfer debit raised by one railway against another takes effect in the respondent railway books only on its acceptance. Until acceptance, the item remains outstanding, because the respondent must verify the debit before adjusting it in its accounts.

q: The Accounts Office of a zonal railway directs stations to remit their earnings promptly, pointing out that keeping 'Cash-in-Transit' low results in the earnings collected being:

options.A: Apportioned among the zonal railways without delay
options.B: Excluded from the gross earnings of the year
options.C: Converted into charged expenditure of the year
options.D: Credited promptly to the account of the Railways with the Reserve Bank of India, improving its cash position

e: Cash-in-Transit represents earnings collected but not yet credited with the Reserve Bank. Keeping it low means earnings are promptly credited to the Railways account with the Reserve Bank of India, improving the cash position and reducing float losses.

q: The expenditure of the Railway Board and of other central organisations of the Railways cannot be attributed directly to any single zonal railway. For purposes such as working out the operating results of the individual railways, this expenditure is distributed among the zonal railways through:
e: Expenditure of the Railway Board and central organisations cannot be directly attributed to any zonal railway. For working out the operating results of individual railways, it is distributed among them through Budget proportions fixed for the purpose.

q: A zonal railway makes its annual appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, the Development Fund and the Pension Fund. In the classification under Major Head 3002, such appropriations to the Railway Funds are booked under:
e: Appropriations from revenue to the Railway Funds, namely the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund and Pension Fund, are classified under Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002, corresponding to the erstwhile Demand for Appropriation to Funds.

q: The cost of diesel fuel consumed by locomotives on a zonal railway is booked by a clerk under Sub-Major Head 07, which covers Operating Expenses — Traffic. Operating Expenses — Fuel are correctly classified under Major Head 3002 as:

options.C: Sub-Major Head 07 itself, as booked by the clerk

e: Under Major Head 3002, Sub-Major Head 08 covers Operating Expenses - Fuel, including the cost of diesel fuel consumed by locomotives. Sub-Major Head 07 covers Operating Expenses - Traffic, so the clerk booking of fuel under 07 is a misclassification.

q: Expenditure on repairs and maintenance of locomotives of a zonal railway is booked by a clerk under Sub-Major Head 04, which covers carriages and wagons. Repairs and Maintenance of Motive Power are correctly classified under Major Head 3002 as:

options.C: Sub-Major Head 04 itself, as booked by the clerk

e: Repairs and Maintenance of Motive Power, that is locomotives, is Sub-Major Head 03 of Major Head 3002. Sub-Major Head 04 covers Repairs and Maintenance of Carriages and Wagons, so booking locomotive repairs under 04 is incorrect.

q: In the classification of railway accounts, a Minor Head is divided, for detailed accounting of expenditure, into:

options.A: Sub-Heads, which are further divided into Detailed Heads
options.B: Plan Heads, which are further divided into Primary Units
options.C: Sub-Major Heads, which are further divided into Major Heads
options.D: Abstracts, which are further divided into Funds

e: In the classification hierarchy, a Minor Head is divided into Sub-Heads for detailed accounting, and Sub-Heads are further divided into Detailed Heads. Primary Units are the object heads applied below this level for expenditure classification.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Primary Units of expenditure are uniform object heads, and the same Primary Unit bears the same meaning under the different Sub-Major Heads of working expenses.
2. A Primary Unit, by itself, indicates the fund from which an item of expenditure is financed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Primary Units are uniform object heads like pay, allowances and materials, and the same Primary Unit has the same meaning under different Sub-Major Heads, so statement 1 is correct. A Primary Unit shows the object of expenditure, not its source of finance, so statement 2 is false.

q: An existing service of the Railways is importantly extended as a result of a fresh policy decision taken by the Government, and the expenditure involved was not contemplated in the approved Budget. Such an important addition to, or extension of, an existing service is treated, for purposes of Parliamentary approval, as a:
e: A New Instrument of Service is an important addition to or extension of an existing service arising from a fresh policy decision and not contemplated in the Budget. It needs Parliamentary approval like a New Service, which is a service not previously sanctioned at all.

q: Expenditure has been incurred by a zonal railway in excess of the grant for a service during a year. Before the Demand for the grant to regularise this excess is presented to the Lok Sabha, the excess expenditure is first examined by the:
e: Excess expenditure over a grant is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee before the Demand for an Excess Grant is presented to the Lok Sabha. This prior scrutiny under Article 115 procedure ensures the excess is justified before regularisation.

q: A clerk, wanting to compare the actual expenditure of a zonal railway for a year with the Final Grant for that year, opens the Finance Accounts of the Railways. The document which actually presents this comparison, together with the explanations of variations, is the:
e: The Appropriation Accounts compare actual expenditure with the Final Grant for the year and explain the variations between them. Finance Accounts only present receipts and disbursements under the Major Heads and make no comparison with grants.

q: While preparing the Balance Sheet of a zonal railway, a clerk proposes to show the accumulated balance of the Pension Fund on the assets side, treating it as an investment of the railway. The accumulated balances of the Railway Funds are correctly shown in the Balance Sheet on the:

options.B: Neither side, the funds being kept outside the Balance Sheet
options.C: Assets side, as proposed by the clerk

e: Railway Funds like the Pension Fund represent amounts owed by the railway to the fund beneficiaries, built up from appropriations. Their accumulated balances are therefore shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet, not as assets of the railway.

q: The accounts of the Government of India are kept in three parts. The transactions of the Contingency Fund of India are recorded in:

options.A: Part I — Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Part II — Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Part III — Public Account of India
options.D: A separate account kept wholly outside the Government accounts

e: Government accounts are kept in three parts: Part I Consolidated Fund, Part II Contingency Fund and Part III Public Account. Transactions of the Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267, are recorded in Part II under Major Head 8000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Part I of the Government accounts, relating to the Consolidated Fund of India, is divided into sections for revenue and capital transactions.
2. Receipts and disbursements on revenue account in Part I are kept distinct from receipts and disbursements on capital account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Part I, the Consolidated Fund, is divided into revenue and capital sections, so statement 1 is correct. Receipts and disbursements on revenue account are kept distinct from those on capital account within Part I, so statement 2 is also correct and both hold.

q: Expenditure is incurred on a work by an officer without the sanction of the authority competent to sanction it, though funds for the work stand allotted in the Budget. In the railway accounts and audit, such expenditure is treated as:
e: Expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure, even if funds stand allotted in the Budget. Allotment of funds and sanction to expenditure are separate requirements, and such items are reported for regularisation.

q: Savings under a head of a zonal railway are formally surrendered during the year after being foreseen. A few months later, a need arises and the railway proposes to treat the surrendered amount as again available for re-appropriation. The correct position is that the amount once surrendered:

options.A: Is no longer available to the railway for re-appropriation during that year
options.B: Remains available for re-appropriation at any time during the year
options.C: Is automatically transferred to the Development Fund
options.D: Can be revived merely by an order of the General Manager

e: Funds once formally surrendered cease to be at the disposal of the railway for that year. A surrendered amount cannot be revived for re-appropriation during the year, as surrender is a definitive giving up of the provision to the Railway Board.

q: A sum provided in the grant of a zonal railway for a service remains wholly unspent at the close of the financial year on 31 March. In the following financial year, this unspent balance:

options.A: Remains at the disposal of the railway for the same service
options.B: Is not available for expenditure, the grant having lapsed at the close of the year, and fresh provision has to be sought if the service is to be continued
options.C: Is carried forward automatically as a suspense balance
options.D: Is credited to the Pension Fund of the Railways

e: Grants lapse at the close of the financial year under the rule of lapse. An amount unspent on 31 March is not available in the next year, and fresh provision must be sought in the next Budget if the service is to be continued.

q: Before the Works Programme of a zonal railway for the following year is finalised, the railway submits its proposals for the works to be included in it, together with their estimated cost, to the Railway Board. These proposals of the railway are known as its:
e: Before the Works Programme is finalised, each railway sends its proposals with estimated costs to the Railway Board; these are its Preliminary Works Programme. After Board scrutiny and selection, the approved works form the Final Works Programme in the Pink Book.

q: In the Works Programme of the Railways, a number of small works of a similar nature are grouped together and provided for under a single combined head, instead of being sanctioned and listed one by one. Works so grouped are known as:

options.D: Lumpsum works of a single work

e: Umbrella works are groups of small works of a similar nature combined and provided for under a single head in the Works Programme, instead of being listed and sanctioned individually. They are later sanctioned in detail within the combined provision as needs arise.

q: For the information of Parliament, the detailed estimates underlying the single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, showing the grant sought under each head of account, are presented in the Budget document known as the:
e: The Detailed Demands for Grants present the detailed estimates under each head of account underlying the single Demand of the Ministry of Railways. They show Parliament the head-wise break-up of the grant sought, unlike the Pink Book which lists works.

q: The Traffic Book of a zonal railway is compiled in two parts. While Part A is concerned with Coaching earnings, Part B of the Traffic Book is concerned with the apportionment of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings among the zonal railways
options.B: Goods earnings among the zonal railways over which the goods traffic has passed
options.C: Capital expenditure among the Plan Heads
options.D: Working expenses among the Sub-Major Heads

e: The Traffic Book is compiled in two parts for apportionment of earnings between railways. Part A deals with Coaching earnings and Part B with Goods earnings apportioned among the zonal railways over which the goods traffic has actually passed.

q: A clerk preparing a statement of the Central Government's accounts proposes to exhibit the External Debt of the Central Government under Major Head 6001 along with the Internal Debt. The correct Major Head for the External Debt of the Central Government is:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, Internal Debt of the Central Government is Major Head 6001 and External Debt is Major Head 6002. Exhibiting external debt under 6001 would mix two distinct debt heads, so 6002 is the correct classification.

q: The Consolidated Fund of India, into which all revenues and loans raised by the Government of India are credited and from which expenditure is met under appropriation made by law, is constituted under the Constitution by:
e: Article 266 of the Constitution constitutes the Consolidated Fund of India, into which all revenues, loans and moneys received in repayment of loans are credited. No money can be withdrawn from it except under appropriation made by law.

q: A doubt is raised in Parliament about the provision of the Constitution which defines a Money Bill and specifies the matters which alone can be dealt with in such a Bill. A Money Bill is defined in:
e: A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Constitution, which lists the matters a Money Bill may contain, such as taxation, government borrowing and charges on the Consolidated Fund. Articles 112 to 114 deal with the Budget and Appropriation Bill procedure.

q: In the Pink Book of the Railways, a number of works of small value are not listed individually, but a consolidated provision is made for them to be sanctioned during the year as the need arises. Such works, provided for through a consolidated provision, are known as:
e: Lumpsum works are small works not listed individually in the Pink Book. A consolidated lumpsum provision is made for them, within which individual works are sanctioned during the year as the need arises, unlike itemised works which are listed by name.

q: A sanctioned work of a zonal railway will remain incomplete at the close of the current year, and a part of its sanctioned cost will still remain to be spent in the following years to complete it. The liability on account of the sanctioned works which is carried over for completion in the future years is known as the:
e: The throw-forward of a work is the liability on sanctioned works that remains to be spent in future years to complete them. It is worked out at Budget time so that provision for works in progress claims priority over new works in the coming year.

q: The sanction accorded to a work of a zonal railway remains incomplete at the close of the financial year and the funds allotted for it during the year remain partly unspent. The correct position in the following year is that:

options.A: The unspent funds do not lapse, but the work requires a fresh provision of funds in the following year's budget for its further execution
options.B: Both the sanction and the unspent funds lapse at the close of the year
options.C: The unspent funds can be spent in the following year without any fresh provision
options.D: The work must be sanctioned afresh before any further expenditure is incurred on it

e: Sanction to a work does not lapse at year-end; only the funds allotted for the year lapse. The incomplete work therefore continues under the same sanction but needs a fresh provision of funds in the following year Budget for its further execution.

q: Under the Constitution, no tax can be levied or collected by the Government except by the authority of law. This principle, which underlies the taxation proposals presented with the Budget, is laid down in:
e: Article 265 of the Constitution lays down that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law. Taxation proposals in the Budget therefore take effect only through the Finance Act passed by Parliament each year.

q: Stores are issued from the stock of a zonal railway for use on a revenue work of the railway. In the Primary Unit (object) classification, stores so issued from stock to revenue works are accounted for under Primary Unit:
e: In the Primary Unit classification, stores issued from stock for use on works are accounted for under Primary Unit 27, which covers materials and stores taken from stock. Direct purchases and suspense adjustments fall under their own separate Primary Units.

q: One zonal railway has to intimate to another zonal railway a transfer transaction which does not involve any actual receipt or payment of cash between the two railways. The advice through which such a transaction is intimated is known as a:
e: A transfer transaction between two railways involving no actual cash movement is advised through a Transfer Without Financial Adjustment. It is an accounting advice only, unlike a Cash Remittance Note which accompanies actual remittance of cash.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a temporary advance from an imprest in railway accounts?

options.A: A temporary advance is given for a specific purpose and is adjusted on completion of that purpose, while an imprest is a standing advance of a fixed amount which is recouped as expenditure is incurred from it
options.B: A temporary advance is a standing advance recouped every month, while an imprest is given only once and is never recouped
options.C: Both a temporary advance and an imprest are permanent advances which are never adjusted
options.D: A temporary advance is held under the Pension Fund, while an imprest is held under the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: A temporary advance is given for a specific purpose and is finally adjusted when that purpose is completed. An imprest is a standing advance of a fixed amount held by an officer and recouped from time to time as expenditure is incurred from it, so option A is correct.

q: A division of a zonal railway proposes to compile and render its own monthly Account Current directly to the Railway Board, treating itself as a separate accounting unit. The correct position is that:

options.A: Every division is an independent accounting unit rendering its own Account Current
options.B: A division renders its Account Current to the Railway Board through the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.C: A division renders a separate Account Current only for capital transactions
options.D: A division is not an independent accounting unit; its transactions are compiled in the accounts of the zonal railway, which renders the Account Current

e: A division is not an independent accounting unit and renders no Account Current of its own. Its transactions are compiled in the books of the zonal railway headquarters, and the zonal railway as a whole renders the monthly Account Current to the Railway Board.

q: An Accounts officer has to refer to the codal provisions governing the accountal of traffic earnings, station accounts and the Traffic Book. These matters are dealt with in:

options.A: Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume I
options.B: Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume II
options.C: Indian Railway Stores Code, Volume II
options.D: Indian Railway Establishment Code, Volume II

e: Traffic earnings, station accounts and the Traffic Book are dealt with in the Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume II. Volume I deals with the general accounts, books and budget matters of the railways, while Volume II covers traffic accounts in detail.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Volume I of the Indian Railway Finance Code contains the general financial rules and procedures, including those relating to sanctions and the budget.
2. Volume II of the Indian Railway Finance Code contains the detailed classification of earnings and expenditure, including the lists of Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Finance Code Volume I contains the general financial rules and procedures, including sanctions and the Budget, so statement 1 is correct. Volume II contains the detailed classification lists of Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units, so both are correct.

q: A railway servant is lent on deputation to an outside organisation, and that organisation pays to the Railways the pension contribution and leave salary contribution in respect of the deputed servant. In the railway accounts, the contributions so recovered are:

options.A: Credited to the revenue (earnings) of the Railways
options.B: Credited to the Capital Fund of the Railways
options.C: Held permanently under a suspense head
options.D: Credited to the Contingency Fund of India

e: Pension and leave salary contributions recovered from an outside organisation for a deputed railway servant are earnings of the Railways. They are credited to revenue as receipts, since the Railways bear the pension and leave liability of the deputed servant.

q: For watching the allotments made and the expenditure incurred under the revenue (ordinary working expenses) heads at the divisional and unit level, the register maintained for allocation control over such revenue expenditure is the:
e: The Revenue Allocation Register is maintained to watch allotments and expenditure under the revenue working expense heads at divisional and unit level. It provides allocation control over revenue expenditure, unlike the Works Register used for works expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Journal Book of a zonal railway, in which transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded, is one of its Subsidiary Books.
2. The Ledger of a zonal railway, in which transactions are posted head-wise from the classified summaries, is one of its General Books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Journal Book, in which transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded, is a Subsidiary Book of original entry, so statement 1 is correct. The Ledger, where transactions are posted head-wise from classified summaries, is a General Book, so both statements are correct.

q: Funds have been allotted in the budget of a zonal railway for a work, but the work has not been sanctioned by the authority competent to sanction it. Expenditure is proposed to be incurred on the ground that funds are available. The correct position is that:

options.A: The allotment of funds in the budget does not by itself authorise the expenditure; the sanction of the competent authority to the work is also necessary
options.B: Availability of funds in the budget is sufficient authority to incur the expenditure
options.C: The expenditure can be incurred and the sanction obtained retrospectively in all cases
options.D: The allotment of funds converts the work into a charged work

e: Allotment of funds in the Budget only provides money; it does not by itself sanction a work or authorise expenditure. The sanction of the competent authority to the estimate is separately necessary before expenditure can be incurred on the work.

q: The estimates of Ordinary Working Expenses of a zonal railway for the ensuing year are initially framed by the executive departments concerned. Before these estimates are adopted in the Budget, they are:

options.B: Audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Sent to the State Governments for their concurrence
options.D: Scrutinised and consolidated by the Accounts Department of the railway

e: Ordinary Working Expenses estimates are framed initially by the executive departments which will spend them. Before adoption in the Budget, they are scrutinised for correctness and classification and consolidated by the Accounts Department of the railway.

q: The Finance Bill introduced in Parliament along with the Budget, which gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Government, is required to be passed by Parliament and to receive the assent of the President within:

options.D: The close of the financial year following its introduction

e: The Finance Bill, which gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Budget, must be passed by Parliament and receive the President assent within 75 days of its introduction. This time limit flows from the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act procedure.

q: Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time and wharfage charges for goods not removed from railway premises within the free time are classified in the railway accounts as part of:

options.D: Traffic Suspense only, and never as earnings

e: Demurrage for detention of wagons beyond free time and wharfage for goods not removed within free time arise directly from goods traffic operations. They are therefore classified as part of Goods earnings, and not as sundry other earnings.

q: A passenger fare collected by a zonal railway is later refunded to the passenger in accordance with the refund rules. In the railway accounts, such a refund of fare is treated as:

options.A: An item of ordinary working expenditure of the railway
options.B: A deduction from (minus entry against) the coaching earnings of the railway
options.C: A charge to the Development Fund
options.D: A deposit payable to the passenger indefinitely

e: A fare refunded to a passenger is not an item of working expenditure. It is treated as a deduction, by a minus entry, from the coaching earnings of the railway, since the earnings originally taken to account for that fare stand reversed.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Liability Register from the Suspense Register in railway accounts?

options.A: Both the registers record only the outstanding balances under the suspense heads
options.B: The Liability Register is maintained by the Cash and Pay Office for cash payments only
options.C: The Suspense Register records the sanctions accorded to works, while the Liability Register records the staff on leave
options.D: The Liability Register watches the liabilities and commitments incurred against grants, while the Suspense Register watches the outstanding items under the suspense heads awaiting final adjustment

e: The Liability Register watches liabilities and commitments incurred against grants so that expenditure does not exceed allotments. The Suspense Register watches outstanding items under suspense heads pending final adjustment, so option D distinguishes the two correctly.

q: It is proposed to open an entirely new Minor Head in the classification of railway accounts to meet a new requirement. Such a new head can be opened only with the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway concerned
options.B: The Railway Board, as the authority competent to amend the classification of accounts
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway concerned

e: The classification of accounts is prescribed in the Finance Code, and a new Minor Head changes that classification. Such a head can be opened only with the sanction of the Railway Board, the authority competent to amend the classification, and not by a zonal officer.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the classification of railway earnings, Coaching earnings are grouped under Abstract A.
2. In the classification of railway earnings, Goods earnings are grouped under Abstract B.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Railway earnings are denoted by the abstracts X, Y and Z, where X is Coaching earnings, Y is Goods earnings and Z is Sundry earnings. Coaching and Goods earnings are therefore not grouped under Abstracts A and B, so neither statement is correct.

q: A section of track is renewed with rails of a heavier section than the existing rails, so that the work partly renews the asset and partly improves it. The correct allocation of the cost of such a work is that:

options.A: The entire cost is charged to Capital, as heavier rails are used
options.B: The entire cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, as it is a renewal
options.C: The entire cost is charged to ordinary working expenses
options.D: The cost of renewal of the asset on a like-for-like basis is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and the additional cost attributable to the improvement or betterment is charged to Capital or the Development Fund, as applicable

e: Where a renewal also improves the asset, the cost is split on a like-for-like basis. The cost of renewing the asset in its original form is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and the extra cost of betterment is charged to Capital or Development Fund.

q: A new railway line is under construction and has not yet been opened for traffic. The interest on the capital invested in the line during the period of its construction is, in the railway accounts:

options.A: Charged to the capital cost of the line during the construction period
options.B: Charged to ordinary working expenses of the open line
options.D: Written off to revenue in the year of construction itself

e: Interest on capital invested in a new line during its construction period is capitalised, that is charged to the capital cost of the line. It becomes part of the cost of the asset created and is not debited to the working expenses of open lines.

q: The monthly accounts of a zonal railway, unlike the accounts of many civil departments which are compiled by the Accountant General, are compiled departmentally. The authority responsible for this departmental compilation of the railway's accounts is:

options.A: The Accountant General of the State in which the railway headquarters is situated
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India directly
options.C: The Accounts Department of the zonal railway itself, headed by its Principal Financial Adviser
options.D: The Pay and Accounts Office of the Ministry of Finance

e: Railway accounts are compiled departmentally by the railway itself, unlike civil departments whose accounts are compiled by the Accountant General. The Accounts Department of the zonal railway, headed by its Principal Financial Adviser, is responsible for this compilation.

q: The cash balance of the Railways held as 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' does not stand in isolation from the finances of the Government of India. In substance, this balance forms part of:

options.A: The cash balance of the State Governments
options.B: The overall cash balance of the Central Government with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: The reserves of the Reserve Bank of India itself
options.D: The Public Account balances of the State Railways only

e: The Railways cash balance held as Deposits with Reserve Bank is a part of the overall cash balance of the Central Government with the Reserve Bank of India. Railway transactions flow through the Government account and do not form a separate banking balance.

q: Recoveries and credits which relate to a head of expenditure, such as credits for stores returned to stock against a work, are not shown as receipts of the Railways. To avoid inflating the expenditure under the head, such credits are exhibited in the accounts as:

options.A: Sundry other earnings of the Railways
options.B: Fresh allotments under the same head
options.D: Deduct (minus) entries under the head of expenditure concerned

e: Credits relating to a head of expenditure, such as stores returned to stock, are shown as deduct or minus entries under that head of expenditure. This avoids inflating both expenditure and receipts, since such recoveries are not earnings of the Railways.

q: The proposals of a zonal railway for the acquisition of locomotives, coaches and wagons for the ensuing year are not shown in a separate budget document of their own. The Rolling Stock Programme, under which such acquisitions are proposed, forms part of:

options.A: The Pink Book of the Railways

e: The Rolling Stock Programme, covering acquisition of locomotives, coaches and wagons for the ensuing year, forms part of the Pink Book of the Railways. The Pink Book presents the Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock programmes together for the year.

q: Which of the following correctly classifies the suspense heads operated in the railway accounts?

options.A: Traffic Suspense and Stores Suspense are both capital suspense heads
options.B: Traffic Suspense is a revenue suspense head, while Stores Suspense and Manufacturing Suspense are capital suspense heads
options.C: Cheques and Bills is a capital suspense head, while Manufacturing Suspense is a revenue suspense head
options.D: All suspense heads in the railway accounts are revenue suspense heads

e: Traffic Suspense arises from revenue traffic transactions and is a revenue suspense head. Stores Suspense and Manufacturing Suspense arise from capital stores and workshop manufacture and are capital suspense heads, so option B classifies them correctly.

q: The Contingency Fund of India, established to meet unforeseen expenditure pending its authorisation by Parliament, is placed at the disposal of:

options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: The Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267, is placed at the disposal of the President of India. Advances are made from it by executive action to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, and are later recouped.

q: A new goods shed is constructed at a station of a zonal railway to improve the facilities for goods traffic. In the investment (Plan Head) classification, this work of providing a traffic facility is classified under:
e: Plan Head 16 covers Traffic Facilities, which includes works like goods sheds, platforms for goods traffic and terminal facilities. A new goods shed to improve goods traffic facilities is therefore classified under Plan Head 16.

q: The Railways pay lease charges to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation for rolling stock leased to them, and a clerk proposes to charge the entire lease charge to Plan Head 22. The correct position is that Plan Head 22 covers only:

options.A: The interest component of the lease charges
options.B: The maintenance component of the lease charges
options.C: The insurance component of the lease charges
options.D: The capital (principal) component of the lease charges, the interest component being charged to revenue

e: Plan Head 22 covers only the capital or principal component of lease charges payable to IRFC for leased rolling stock. The interest component of the lease charges is a revenue charge and is not booked under Plan Head 22, so the clerk proposal is wrong.

q: At the Revised Estimates stage, a zonal railway revises its estimate of expenditure for the year upwards, and an officer proposes to incur expenditure up to the revised figure even though it exceeds the grant allotted. The correct position is that:

options.A: The Revised Estimates themselves authorise expenditure up to the revised figure
options.B: The Revised Estimates are only a revised assessment of requirements; expenditure remains limited to the grant and allotments actually authorised
options.C: Expenditure in excess of the grant becomes charged expenditure at the Revised Estimates stage
options.D: The Revised Estimates dispense with the need for a supplementary grant in all cases

e: Revised Estimates are only a revised assessment of the requirements of the year; they do not themselves authorise any expenditure. Expenditure remains limited to the grant voted and the allotments actually authorised, and excess needs a supplementary grant.

q: A lathe and other machinery are purchased for installation in an existing workshop of a zonal railway, and a clerk proposes to book the cost under Plan Head 42 along with the workshop buildings. Machinery and Plant, as distinct from the workshop buildings themselves, are correctly classified under:
e: Machinery and Plant, including lathes and other workshop machinery, is classified under Plan Head 41. Plan Head 42 covers Workshops including production units, that is the workshop buildings and structures, and not the machinery installed in them.

q: A recreation club building and a community hall are constructed by a zonal railway for the welfare of its staff. In the investment (Plan Head) classification, such works of amenities for staff are classified under:
e: Plan Head 52 covers Amenities for Staff, which includes welfare works like recreation clubs, community halls, schools and hospitals for staff. Staff quarters themselves fall under Plan Head 51, so a recreation club building is classified under Plan Head 52.

q: The platform surface of a station is raised and extended, and additional platform shelters are provided for the convenience of passengers. In the investment (Plan Head) classification, such works of passenger amenities are classified under:
e: Plan Head 53 covers Passenger Amenities at stations, such as raised platforms, platform extensions, shelters and waiting facilities for passengers. Such works are therefore classified under Plan Head 53 and not under staff or traffic facility heads.

q: The panel interlocking installation at a station of a zonal railway is replaced by a modern electronic interlocking system. In the investment (Plan Head) classification, this signalling work is classified under:
e: Signalling and Telecommunication works are classified under Plan Head 33. Replacement of panel interlocking by electronic interlocking is a signalling work, so it falls under Plan Head 33, whether it is a renewal or a new work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores Suspense and Manufacturing Suspense are operated in the capital section of the railway accounts.
2. Cheques and Bills and Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are operated in the revenue section of the railway accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Stores Suspense and Manufacturing Suspense are operated in the capital section, so statement 1 is correct. Cheques and Bills is a remittance head and not a revenue suspense head, so statement 2 as framed is not correct and only statement 1 holds.

q: The Subsidiary Books of a zonal railway, in which transactions are entered in detail in the first instance before their classification and summarisation, are also described as the:
e: Subsidiary Books are the books in which transactions are entered in detail in the first instance, such as the Cash Book and Journal Book. They are therefore called books of original entry, from which classified summaries and General Books are later built up.

q: A sum appropriated during a year to the Depreciation Reserve Fund remains partly unspent at the close of that year. Unlike the balance of a grant, the unspent balance of the Fund at the close of the year:

options.A: Lapses and is credited back to revenue
options.B: Is surrendered to the General Revenues
options.C: Is transferred to the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Does not lapse; it is carried forward in the Fund for utilisation in the following years

e: Balances of the Depreciation Reserve Fund do not lapse at the close of the year. The unspent balance is carried forward in the Fund and remains available for renewal and replacement works in the following years, unlike a Budget grant which lapses.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh was set up as a dedicated safety fund with a corpus to be built up over a period of years, so that safety works are not held up for want of annual budgetary provision. A distinguishing feature of the balances of this fund is that they are:

options.A: Lapsable at the close of every financial year
options.B: Credited to the Pension Fund at the close of every year
options.C: Available only for works on strategic lines
options.D: Non-lapsable, and are carried forward for expenditure on safety works

e: Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh balances are non-lapsable by design, so that the dedicated safety corpus built up over the years is not lost at year-end. The balances are carried forward and spent only on safety-related works of the Railways.

q: In the Debt Head Report of a zonal railway, the balances under the remittance heads, such as Remittances into Banks and Cheques and Bills, are exhibited:

options.A: As a part of the revenue receipts of the railway
options.B: As a part of the capital outlay of the railway
options.C: As a distinct group of heads, separate from both the debt heads and the suspense heads
options.D: Only in the Balance Sheet, and not in the Debt Head Report

e: In the Debt Head Report, balances under remittance heads like Remittances into Banks and Cheques and Bills are shown as a distinct group. Remittances are neither debt heads nor suspense heads, and the report therefore exhibits them separately.

q: A Budget document presented with the Union Budget sets out, against the money provided for each scheme, the physical deliverables expected to be achieved with that money during the year. This document, which links financial outlays to expected outcomes, is the:
e: The Outcome Budget links financial outlays provided for each scheme with the physical deliverables or outcomes expected from that money during the year. It is presented with the Union Budget to show what results the expenditure is intended to produce.

q: On the last day allotted for voting of the Demands for Grants, the Speaker puts all the outstanding Demands to the vote of the Lok Sabha together, whether they have been discussed or not. This procedure is known as the:
e: On the last allotted day for voting of Demands, the Speaker puts all outstanding Demands together to the vote of the Lok Sabha, whether discussed or not. This procedure for disposing of the remaining Demands at one stroke is called the Guillotine.

q: In the Railway Codes, amendments to the text of a Code are issued from time to time through correction slips. The abbreviation 'ACS', used for such a slip, stands for:
e: In the Railway Codes, ACS stands for Advance Correction Slip. Amendments to the Codes are issued through such slips, which are later incorporated in the Code text, and each slip bears its own number and date for reference and record.

q: A change is required in the list of Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units prescribed for the classification of railway accounts. Such amendments and corrections to the classification lists in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through:
e: Amendments and corrections to the classification lists of Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through Correction Slips. Budget circulars and Pink Book entries cannot change the prescribed classification.

q: Certain items of expenditure, such as the expenditure of the Railway Board and of audit offices, cannot be attributed directly to any one zonal railway. The device by which such expenditure is distributed among the zonal railways for inclusion in their estimates is known as:
e: Expenditure like that of the Railway Board and audit offices, which cannot be attributed to one zonal railway, is distributed among the zonal railways through Budget proportions. These proportions are used for including such distributable expenditure in railway estimates.

q: The integrated computer application on the Railways which brings together the payroll work of the staff with the billing, books and budget work of the Accounts Department is known by the abbreviation 'IPAS', which stands for:
e: IPAS stands for Integrated Payroll and Accounting System. It is the integrated application that combines staff payroll with the billing, books and budget work of the Accounts Department on the Railways, replacing the earlier separate applications.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Once the accounts of a month have been closed, further entries can be passed in that month at any time during the same financial year.
2. A rectification relating to a month whose accounts have been closed is carried out through entries in a subsequent month whose accounts are still open.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Once the accounts of a month are closed, no further entries can be passed in that month, so statement 1 is false. A rectification for a closed month is carried out through transfer entries in a subsequent month whose accounts are still open, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: At the close of the financial year, every officer who operates a suspense head on a zonal railway is required to furnish a certificate to the Accounts Office. This certificate relates to:

options.A: The budget allotment required by his office for the next year
options.B: The earnings of the units working under him
options.C: The staff strength of his office
options.D: The review, and the correctness, of the outstanding balances under the suspense heads operated by him

e: At the close of the financial year, every officer operating a suspense head must certify the review and correctness of the outstanding balances under the suspense heads operated by him. This certificate supports the Debt Head Report and year-end clearance of suspense items.

q: A journal (transfer) adjustment has to be carried out in the books of a zonal railway to correct the allocation of an item. The document through which such a transfer adjustment is authorised and recorded is called a:
e: A transfer adjustment in the books, such as correction of a wrong allocation, is authorised and recorded through a Transfer Entry Order. The order supports the journal entry passed in the Journal Book for adjusting the amount between the heads concerned.

q: The total capital outlay of a zonal railway, as exhibited in its Block Account, is periodically agreed and reconciled with the:

options.A: Budget Register maintained in the Accounts Office
options.B: Pink Book maintained in the Railway Board
options.C: Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments
options.D: Contractor's ledgers maintained by the executive departments

e: The capital outlay in the Block Account is periodically agreed with the Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments. This reconciliation ensures that every asset created is recorded both in the accounts and in the departmental asset records.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, Major Heads 8658 (Suspense Accounts), 8675 (Deposits with Reserve Bank) and 8670 (Cheques and Bills) all fall under the Public Account section relating to:
e: Major Heads 8658 Suspense Accounts, 8675 Deposits with Reserve Bank and 8670 Cheques and Bills all fall in the Public Account under the Suspense and Miscellaneous section of the List of Major and Minor Heads, which groups suspense and miscellaneous balances pending final clearance (8782 Cash Remittances, by contrast, sits in the separate Remittances section).

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, a receipt or item of expenditure which is not covered by any specific minor head is generally accommodated under the minor head bearing the code:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, the minor head code 800 is the residual head, generally titled Other Expenditure or Other Receipts. Any item not covered by a specific minor head is accommodated under minor head 800 of the Major Head concerned.

q: The Economic Survey, which reviews the state of the economy, is presented to Parliament:

options.A: Along with the Appropriation Accounts of the year
options.B: At the end of the financial year
options.D: Shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget

e: The Economic Survey reviews the state of the economy and the performance of the major sectors during the year. It is presented to Parliament shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget, providing the background to the Budget proposals.

q: The amount appropriated each year from revenue to the Railway Pension Fund is not fixed arbitrarily; it is assessed with reference to:

options.A: The gross earnings of the year
options.B: The actuarial valuation of the pension liability
options.C: The dividend liability of the Railways
options.D: The balance available in the Development Fund

e: The annual appropriation to the Railway Pension Fund is assessed with reference to the actuarial valuation of the pension liability of the Railways. This ensures the Fund is built up on a scientific basis to meet the future pension payments of retired staff.

q: The expenditure of a zonal railway on its hospitals and other health services for staff is booked by a clerk under Sub-Major Head 10 of Major Head 3002, which covers Miscellaneous Working Expenses. Such expenditure on hospitals and health services is correctly classified under Sub-Major Head:
e: Expenditure on hospitals and health services for staff is part of staff welfare and is classified under Sub-Major Head 09 of Major Head 3002. Sub-Major Head 10 covers Miscellaneous Working Expenses, so the clerk booking under 10 is incorrect.

q: Besides authorising the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, the Appropriation Act also contains:

options.A: The taxation proposals of the Government for the year
options.B: The list of works included in the Pink Book
options.C: The report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: A Schedule specifying the services and purposes and the amounts appropriated for each of them

e: Besides authorising withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, the Appropriation Act carries a Schedule. The Schedule specifies the services and purposes and the maximum amounts appropriated for each, covering both voted grants and charged expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross Budgetary Support provided to the Railways forms part of their Capital-at-charge.
2. Extra Budgetary Resources raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation also form part of the Capital-at-charge of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Gross Budgetary Support given to the Railways is Government capital and forms part of their Capital-at-charge, so statement 1 is correct. Extra Budgetary Resources raised through IRFC are lease finances serviced by the Railways and do not form part of Capital-at-charge, so only 1 holds.

q: The Debt Head Report of a zonal railway, showing the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, is rendered:

options.A: Annually, along with the Appropriation Accounts
options.B: Monthly, along with the Account Current
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year

e: The Debt Head Report, showing balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, is rendered monthly along with the Account Current to the Railway Board. Monthly rendering helps watch and clear outstanding suspense and debt head balances promptly.

q: The balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' appearing in the books of a zonal railway is reconciled periodically with:

options.A: The Cash Book of the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: The Asset Registers of the executive departments
options.C: The figures intimated by the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Pink Book maintained in the Railway Board

e: The balance under Deposits with Reserve Bank in the railway books is reconciled periodically with the figures intimated by the Reserve Bank of India. Agreement with the Bank figures proves the correctness of the cash balance shown in the railway accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The initial records of the transactions of a railway, such as bills, vouchers and measurement books, are prepared by the executive departments.
2. The Accounts Department itself prepares all the initial records of the transactions of a railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Initial records like bills, vouchers and measurement books originate in the executive departments which execute the transactions, so statement 1 is correct. The Accounts Department checks, classifies and accounts for them but does not itself prepare all initial records, so only 1 holds.

q: Although the fare or freight for traffic booked at a station may be collected later, the earnings of the Railways are brought to account:

options.A: Only when the cash is actually received at the station
options.B: Only at the close of the financial year
options.C: On the basis of the Budget Estimates for the year
options.D: On the basis of the traffic booked, irrespective of when the cash is collected

e: Railway earnings are accounted for on the basis of traffic booked, that is on accrual, irrespective of when the fare or freight is actually collected. Amounts not yet collected are held under Traffic Suspense or Demands Recoverable till realisation.

q: A member of the Lok Sabha wishes to move a cut motion in respect of an item of expenditure. A cut motion cannot be moved in respect of:

options.A: A Demand for Grant relating to working expenses
options.B: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: A Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways

e: Cut motions can be moved only on voted Demands for Grants. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament under Article 113, so no cut motion can be moved in respect of charged expenditure.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), the dedicated fund for safety-related works of the Railways, is financed through:

options.A: A surcharge on passenger fares only
options.C: Gross Budgetary Support and the internal resources of the Railways
options.D: Fines and penalties collected by the Railways

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is financed through Gross Budgetary Support from the Government and the internal resources of the Railways. It is not financed by a fare surcharge alone or by IRFC borrowings alone, so option C states its funding correctly.

q: A work is included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) of a zonal railway but has not yet been sanctioned by the competent authority. For such a work, the provision made in the Budget is only:

options.B: The full estimated cost of the work
options.C: A provision under a suspense head
options.D: No provision of any kind is permissible

e: A work included in the Pink Book but not yet sanctioned by the competent authority can receive only a token provision in the Budget. The full provision is made only after sanction, since expenditure cannot be incurred on an unsanctioned work beyond the token stage.

q: Land is acquired for the construction of a sanctioned railway work. The cost of the land so acquired is treated in the accounts as:

options.A: A charge on the working expenses of the year of acquisition
options.B: A permanent debit under a suspense head
options.C: A debit to the Depreciation Reserve Fund in all cases
options.D: Part of the capital cost of the work

e: Land acquired for a sanctioned railway work is a part of the cost of creating that asset. Its cost is therefore treated as part of the capital cost of the work and charged to the same source of finance as the work, and not to working expenses.

q: The Appropriation Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha after the Demands for Grants have been voted to authorise withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, is categorised as:
e: The Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill, as it deals with withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, a matter listed in Article 110. It is introduced only in the Lok Sabha after the Demands for Grants have been voted by it.

q: The Appropriation Bill becomes the Appropriation Act, authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, on receiving the assent of:

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The Appropriation Bill becomes the Appropriation Act on receiving the assent of the President. Only after this assent can money be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India under the authority of the Act for the services voted and charged.

q: After the Budget has been presented to Parliament, the stage which follows before the Demands for Grants are taken up for detailed examination and voting is:

options.A: The passing of the Finance Bill
options.B: The passing of the Appropriation Bill
options.C: The presentation of the Appropriation Accounts
options.D: A general discussion on the Budget in both Houses

e: After the Budget is presented, a general discussion on the Budget takes place in both Houses before the Demands are taken up. Only after this general discussion do the Demands for Grants go to the Departmental Standing Committees and then to voting in the Lok Sabha.

q: The Budget document which presents, in a nutshell, a brief summary of the Budget showing receipts, expenditure and the various deficit indicators is:
e: Budget at a Glance is the document that presents a brief summary of the Budget in a nutshell. It shows receipts, expenditure and the various deficit indicators like revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit at one place for quick reference.

q: To raise resources from the capital market for financing the acquisition of rolling stock, the Railways set up a dedicated borrowing company, the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC). This corporation was set up in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation was set up in 1986 as the dedicated market borrowing arm of the Railways. It raises funds from the capital market to finance acquisition of rolling stock, which is leased to the Railways against lease charges.
